events.text: It acts as the authoritative transaction ledger exposure layer for a given positionkeepingid (Account Instance Reference).

rows: Ledger-level transaction entries — identification, date, description, amount, debit/credit indicator, status
Manage customer profile data — belongs to Party Directory SD
Manage product agreement configuration — belongs to Sales Product Agreement SD
Maintain customer holdings registry — belongs to Customer Product & Service Directory SD
Perform payment execution — belongs to Payment Execution domain
Authoritative transaction ledger exposure layer — read-only in current scope
Account Instance Reference — unique identifier per account position record

events.text: The existing FinancialTransactionCapture BQ is used. No new Behaviour Qualifier was introduced. All enhancements remain within the existing BIAN structure.

rows: 1..* — Multiple transaction entries can exist under the same Position Keeping CR. Each entry is independently addressable via financialtransactioncaptureid in the path.

financialtransactioncaptureid — BIAN-standard BQ instance identifier. In this implementation, both positionkeepingid and financialtransactioncaptureid are passed with the same account number (to preserve BIAN endpoint structure without deviation).
Initiate, Update, Control, Initiate CR, Position Recalculation

events.text: 3. When to Use This Service Domain
This SD is invoked when transaction-level history retrieval is required for a specific account. Current scope supports read-only retrieval only.

rows: Transaction History View Customer opens Transaction History screen in mobile/internet banking.

Call GET /.../FinancialTransactionCapture/{id}/Retrieve with fromDate, toDate, and pageSize query parameters. Fetches transactions within the date range with pagination support for infinite scroll UI.
Statement Generation Customer requests account statement for a defined period.
Invoke the same Retrieve endpoint with fromDate = statement start date and toDate = statement end date. Returned transactions are compiled into a statement document.
Operational or Audit Review Operations or audit team reviewing account activity.
Retrieve endpoint invoked with date filters and pageSize for controlled, paginated result extraction. Supports reconciliation and audit.

events.text: This is an Operational Ledger Exposure Domain. Each transaction entry must capture:

rows: Unique identifier for each ledger entry — for internal reference and audit traceability
Booking date of the transaction — when it was posted to the ledger
Human-readable description — merchant name, reference, or payment description
Explicit monetary value of the ledger entry with currency — no ambiguity of implicit values
Explicit classification of transaction direction (Debit/Credit) — avoids relying on positive/negative amount inference
Status of the transaction (e.g. Completed / Rejected) — derived from upstream posting system status
BIAN enum value for status — Completed / Rejected / Initiated etc.
Client batch ID from the posting system — provides traceability back to the originating posting batch

events.text: The following query parameters are supported on the Retrieve endpoint to filter and paginate transaction results:

rows: Start date for transaction filtering — only transactions on or after this date are returned
End date for transaction filtering — only transactions on or before this date are returned
Maximum number of transaction records to return per call — supports paginated UI / infinite scroll
The API response must include next page and previous page tokens to support subsequent paginated calls when the result count exceeds pageSize.

events.text: The following enhancements were introduced while preserving Service Domain boundaries:

rows: Explicit monetary value of the ledger entry using a structured Amount object including currency. Avoids ambiguity of implicit amount fields.
Enum: Debit / Credit. Provides explicit classification of transaction direction. Avoids relying on positive/negative amount sign inference. Ensures semantic clarity for consuming systems.
BQ is modeled with cardinality 1..* — multiple transaction entries exist under the same CR, each independently addressable via financialtransactioncaptureid.
Added to the Retrieve endpoint to support date-range filtering and result pagination.
next page and previous page tokens must be returned in the response to support subsequent paginated calls.
This SD does not require its own schema. It connects directly to the core target adapter to pull transactions from the core posting system.

events.text: All enhancements remain within Position Keeping SD scope and do not violate service domain boundaries:

rows: Represents ledger-level transaction data only — not customer or product data
Does not introduce payment initiation or posting orchestration — belongs to Payment Execution domain
Does not perform ledger recalculation or accounting — that belongs to accounting domains
Position Keeping exposes results of completed postings — it does not execute them
Unique identifier assigned to the financial transaction/posting instruction.
Narrative or business description explaining the purpose of the transaction.
Indicates whether the transaction is a debit or credit posting.
Monetary amount associated with the financial transaction.
Currency code representing the denomination of the transaction amount.
Date and time when the transaction was booked or processed.
Current processing or operational status reason associated with the transaction/posting batch.
Classification of the transaction status such as initiated, completed, rejected, or pending.
Unique identifier assigned to the posting event or posting instruction batch.
